<div class="card card-retractable" style="margin-bottom: 2rem;" onclick="this.classList.toggle('expanded')">

  <p style="text-align: center;font-weight: bold; font-size: 28px;">
  Challenges
  </p>
  The mindset behind GPMelt development was to create a tool which is flexible enough to deal with a great variety of existing - and to come !- TPP experimental set-ups. 
  
  - **Flexibility often comes at the cost of complexity**, and requires a **deeper understanding than a black box**.
  - To allow for flexibility, numerous parameters have been left free to be chosen or adapted by the user. However, **informed parameter choices** requires an additional step of understanding, through visualisation and intuition of how a parameter value impacts the model output.
  - Users (biologists, bioinformaticians) often risk treating tools as black boxes and spontaneouly **use default parameters without knowing** how - nor why - to adapt them. 

  The challenge was to design a **tutorial that promotes understanding, not just execution.**
  </div>


<div class="card-row">

  <div class="card card-retractable" onclick="this.classList.toggle('expanded')">
  <p style="text-align: center;font-weight: bold; font-size: 28px;">
  Approach
  </p>
  I designed a step-by-step, interactive tutorial combining **practical usage with conceptual guidance**.

  Key elements:

  - structured workflow:
    - data preparation;
    - parameters selection;
    - output interpretation;
  - **copy-paste ready code** to reduce friction;
  - integration of **high-quality visual outputs**, with explanations and code on how to generate them;
  - tight coupling between:
    - practice (how to use the tool);
    - theory (why it works this way).
  
  Users can progressively **move from usage to deeper understanding.**
  
  </div>

  <div class="card card-retractable" onclick="this.classList.toggle('expanded')">
  <p style="text-align: center;font-weight: bold; font-size: 28px;">
  Strengths
  </p>
  - Ability to teach complex technical tools to non-expert users;
  - design of structured, user-centered learning experiences;
  - bridging theory and practice in a usable way;
  - encouraging user **autonomy and critical use of tools**;
  - clear communication of data workflows and outputs.
  </div>

</div>

<div class="card card-retractable" style="margin-bottom: 2rem;" onclick="this.classList.toggle('expanded')">

  <p style="text-align: center;font-weight: bold; font-size: 28px;">
  Impact
  </p>
  GPMelt has always been developped with the deep wish to be an **actionable statistical framework**, not just a black box. <br>
  In the course of my PhD, I encountered a lot of dataset and experimental design that would have beneficiating from GPMelt's hierarchical modelling. Thus, I envisioned this tool with the power to analyse more than just TPP data. However,this required to leave enough parametrical freedom to better accomodate for the specificity of different data types and experimental designs. <br>
  This tutorial supported onboarding of new users, and **demonstrated all the capabilities of the tool, with the hope to inspire users**: while previous experimental designs were restricted to available statistical framework for analysis, **GPMelt allows for creativity and novelty to design complex new experiments**, pionnering new discoveries !
</div>
